note_sections.t: Rising prostate-specific antigen (4.8 ng/mL) combined with a confirmed ISUP GG 4 result from a previous biopsy procedure.

Investigated initially for an incidental prostate-specific antigen elevation in the middle of 2023, this 65-year-old individual subsequently received a positive biopsy result confirming ISUP GG 4 disease. He works as a retired carpenter, resides with his partner, and reports being never married. A non-smoker with no active medications or comorbid conditions, he maintains a regular cycling regimen five days weekly and restricts alcohol to four units per week. Lower urinary tract symptoms remain minimal, reflected by an International Prostate Symptom Score of 3 out of 35, and he explicitly denies hematuria or pelvic discomfort. His clinical background is otherwise unremarkable aside from a recent dermatology visit for actinic keratosis screening. Commuting over an hour by train, he favors flexible scheduling to accommodate his travel routine.

DRE — texture: firm, discrete nodule palpable in the right lobe; mobility: unrestricted; asymmetry: noted only at the nodular site, with the remainder of the gland presenting symmetrically and smooth. Vital parameters demonstrate stability, registering a blood pressure of 129/75 mmHg and a heart rate of 56 bpm. Systemic inspection reveals no palpable lymphadenopathy or abdominal abnormalities.
